The rail system is assumed to follow the mechanical property of Bernoulli-Euler beam, the detail modeling method can be consulted in Ref. [28].

In this present study, the track model is constructed by FEM, in which the rail is modelled as Bernoulli-Euler beam, the track slab is modelled as thin-plate element, the rail pad is modelled as discrete supports of spring and dashpot, and the track slab and the subgrade are connected by continuous plane springs and dashpots.
The rail is modeled by Bernoulli-Euler beam and Timonshenko beam respectively, and the rail-track interaction is equivalently represented by the spring-dashpot elements.

Here, the rail and the bridge girder, the track slab, and the bridge pier are firstly modelled as the Bernoulli-Euler beam, thin-plate and rotatable bar, respectively, and all track structures (rail and slab track) and substructures (bridge girder and pier) are coupled by spring-dashpot elements.
As shown in Fig. 2, the rail is modeled as Bernoulli-Euler beam, and the track slab and concrete baseplate are modeled as Mindlin plate el ements and double-beam elements, respectively.
The track is regarded as an elastic system with three layers including the rail modelled by spatial Bernoulli-Euler beam, track slab and basement modelled by thin-plate element.
